result.summary: Reject node startup when automatic Tor listening is active and explicit `-bind` parameters are set without a dedicated, non-wildcard onion bind (`-bind=<addr>=onion`). Wildcard onion binds are also explicitly rejected during initialization.
result.problem: When automatic onion service creation (`-listenonion`) lacks a dedicated onion bind, Tor forwards incoming connections to the node's primary listening socket. Bitcoin Core cannot distinguish these from direct IP connections, misclassifying peers and potentially granting anonymous Tor peers whitelist permissions assigned to the Tor daemon's local IP address.
evidence: Commit 1c18c977e0 and description state that Tor peers arriving through shared or wildcard binds inherit IP-based whitelist permissions, implementing the recommendation from closed PR #34892.
Release notes highlight that because `-listenonion` defaults to true when listening, existing configurations specifying only standard `-bind` options will fail to start until updated.
result.scope_notes: Breaking configuration change: any node running with explicit `-bind` options will fail startup on upgrade unless it adds a `-bind=<addr>=onion` listener or explicitly sets `-listenonion=0`.
result.changed_since_previous: Added an explicit check and startup failure for wildcard onion binds (`b.IsBindAny()`), added an early check in `AppInitParameterInteraction`, and updated documentation and release notes.
result.card: PR 36170 causes bitcoind to refuse startup if automatic Tor listening is enabled alongside explicit -bind options unless a dedicated, non-wildcard onion bind is specified. Without a dedicated bind, incoming Tor connections land on standard sockets where they cannot be distinguished from direct connections, risking inadvertent whitelisting of anonymous Tor peers with permissions assigned to the Tor daemon IP. Because -listenonion is enabled by default, existing configurations using -bind will need to add an onion bind or pass -listenonion=0.

risk.why: Stricter startup validation will prevent existing nodes that use custom -bind options from booting after upgrade until their configuration is adjusted.
